topic.title: Why Rent Keeps Going Up
topic.hook: Supply, zoning, who sets the price
topic.payoff: Supply, zoning, who sets the price

copy.title: WHY YOUR RENT NEVER STOPS CLIMBING

steps.rule: Count who controls the land supply
steps.why: zoning boards cap new units, so scarcity is a policy choice, not an accident.

steps.rule: Map who sits on that board
steps.why: existing property owners vote against new builds because more supply lowers their asset price.
twelve renters competing for ten units lets the landlord raise price without adding a single brick.
higher rents lift assessed values, which lift the portfolio the board members already own.
when the people who profit from scarcity also vote on whether to end it, the scarcity compounds.

copy.kicker: The price is set before you ever apply
copy.thumb_scene: Wick stands on a plain white studio background, arms crossed, one hand holding a single red brick at chest height, a small laminated zoning map pinned to the brick with a thumbtack, his expression flat and certain, nothing else in frame.
copy.send_to: the friend who just got hit with a rent hike and has no idea why
